utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-14 & 14/2-R77, the Prosecutor versus Josip Jovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. May I have the appearances. When I say "Prosecution," I usually say "Prosecution first." Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. David Akerson on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor, and I'm here with Rebecca Graham, Sebastiaan van Hooydonk, and Salvatore Cannata.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Akerson. It seems that no one has appeared for the Defence. That means neither the accused. Therefore, it's perhaps important to establish what the present situation is. Mr. Jovic has been summoned to appear today. Mr. Jovic, through counsel, has filed on the 23rd of September, although I have not the registered copy, but I have a courtesy copy before me at this moment, a motion of the accused Josip Jovic for postponement of the Initial Appearance. I was informed that, again through counsel, Mr. Jovic has been informed that the motion was denied. Nevertheless, Mr. Jovic did not appear today. Could either the registrar or the Prosecution give me any further information as to what happened, apart from what I just said. Was there any additional message received from Mr. Jovic or counsel? Mr. Akerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: The Prosecution has heard nothing from Defence counsel or from the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the registrar received any message?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, I'll briefly explain the reasons why Mr. Jovic asked for postponement. Mr. Jovic has asked for postponement, but first of all, it was stated in the motion that he received -- that a summons was served upon the accused to appear. That means that there could be at this moment no doubt about his awareness of the Initial Appearance to take place today. The main reason for Mr. Jovic to ask for postponement is that he considers it his right to first, under Croatian law, use all the legal remedies at his disposal in order to see whether there's any duty for him to cooperate with the Tribunal. Mr. Jovic claims that the Tribunal has no jurisdiction, although he does not in this motion explain why he takes this position. And he first wants, under the Croatian constitution and under the Croatian laws, have established whether he is under a duty to cooperate, which seems to mean that Mr. Jovic considers this on the basis of the determination of Croatian courts rather than on the determination of this Tribunal, that it should be established whether this Tribunal has jurisdiction. The usual way of challenging jurisdiction is to appear before the court that is involved in the matter and then to challenge the jurisdiction of that court. Under the present circumstances, it is established that Mr. Jovic has not appeared, that Mr. Jovic is aware of the Initial Appearance, and that the Trial Chamber will consider what measures to take under the present circumstances. One obvious measure to be considered, to issue a warrant of arrest. Is there anything the Prosecution would like to submit at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Although we were not looking to have Mr. Jovic taken into custody, we had issued a summons and we were hoping that he would appear. But since he has not asked for a delay in these proceedings based on his inability to be here but challenging the jurisdiction, we would ask that an arrest warrant be issued and then we can address the issue of bond when he appears at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does the Office of the Prosecution intend to make any written submissions on it? I mean, I'm not specifically asking for it, but on the other way, if you think it would be better for you to make any written submissions, of course we would consider them. Otherwise, the Chamber would consider this oral application for an arrest warrant by a bond upon appearance should be discussed to be a sufficient basis for issuing any order, including the one you were just asking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I think the issue is so straightforward and simple, Your Honour, that I don't believe that we could benefit the Court by filing a written submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll not wait for any written submissions and the Chamber will consider what step to take. Is there any other matter to be raised at this moment? If not, then we'll stand adjourned, sine die.
